title: Ongota language - Wikipedia
text: Ongota is a moribund language of southwest Ethiopia. UNESCO reported in 2012 that out of a total ethnic population of 115, only 12 elderly native speakers remained, the rest of their small village on the west bank of the Weito River having adopted the Tsamai language instead.

title: Ongota language
text: The Ongota language is spoken by a very small number of elderly individuals in southwest Ethiopia. According to a 2012 UNESCO report, only 12 native speakers remained at that time, all elderly, out of an ethnic Ongota population of 115.

title: Ongota: The Hidden Language of Ethiopia | Language Learners Hub
text: The greatest mystery in Ongota history is within their language. It does not fit neatly into Ethiopia’s main language families: Afroasiatic or Nilo-Saharan. Some linguists argue it is a unique isolate, while others believe centuries of cultural contact shaped it into a hybrid tongue.

title: (PDF) The Ongota language – and two ways of looking at the history...
text: The Ongota language is critically endangered, with only about ten elders still speaking it. Ongota community of approximately 100 individuals resides in Muts’e, Southwest Ethiopia.

title: Documentation of Ongota | Endangered Languages Archive
text: It is likely a language isolate. The divergent character of Ongota and its retention of genetically heterogeneous lexical elements make the classification of the language highly problematic. Bender (1994), shows that Ongota cannot be paralleled to any neighbouring group.

title: Ongota Language (BXE) – L1 & L2 Speakers... | Ethnologue Free
text: Ongota is an endangered indigenous language of Ethiopia. It is an isolate that is not known to be related to any other language. The language is used as a first language by the elderly only.

title: The documentation of Ongota: a linguistic isolate of... | Culture in Crisis
text: The language defies classification and is considered an isolate. Investigating the origins of Ongota and its community will provide important insight into African linguistic diversity and history.

title: Critically Endangered Languages — Simpson Soft UK Limited
text: The Ongota oral tradition comprises poems, legends, tales, myths, proverbs and riddles transmitted in the Ongota language, which has no written script. The people are mostly hunter-gatherers and one of the reasons for the decline of the language is a loss of livelihood.
